Date: Fri, 18 Sep 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity sourcing playbook + SLA asks — HelioGen

Hi Alice / HelioGen team,

Thanks again for the time earlier — quickly capturing what we heard and the concrete next steps so nothing slips. Short summary first, then an explicit action map.

What we heard (pain & constraints)
- Production latency spikes at tail (p95 ~ 900–1,200ms) impacting user-facing autocomplete and endpoint SLAs.
- Multi-tenant noise: internal data sensitivity (PHI in prompts) requires strong isolation and auditability.
- Bursty workload (training inference + nightly batch embeddings) — needs steady reserved capacity with burst windows.
- Procurement / security gate: SOC2 evidence & KMS integration are gating to a pilot.

Goals you stated
- Predictable throughput for peak production: ~2–3M tokens/day with sustained concurrent inference for 200 qps.
- Latency targets: p50 < 80ms, p95 < 350ms (for 1k token avg requests).
- Isolation: tenant-level network and workload segmentation, audit logs, and customer-managed keys preferred.
- Timeline: procurement approval by end of October; pilot in November.

What we propose (high level)
- Dedicated reserved pool: 4 H100-equivalent nodes with tenant isolation (dedicated compute lane + VPC peering) and burst capacity (additional 2 nodes for short windows).
- Autoscale policy: steady baseline + rule-based burst for nightly batch jobs; canary traffic ramp for rollouts.
- Performance controls: KV prefix caching for common prompts, request-level batching, and quantization profiles to reduce token cost while meeting latency SLOs.
- Security: KMS/HSM integration, encrypted logs, and SOC2 artefacts.

Action map (owners + dates)
1) Architecture workshop (60–90m) — goal: finalize node sizing, network (VPC) patterns, and fallback model policy. Owner: Marissa. Proposed dates: Sep 22 or Sep 24.
2) Security questionnaire + SOC2 evidence handoff — Owner: Tessa. Target: Sep 29.
3) Procurement estimate & term sheet (preliminary) — Owner: Ben. Deliverable: cost estimate and SLA bullets. Target: Oct 2.
4) Pilot kickoff checklist (ops & runbook) — deliverable after workshop.

Attachments included: redwood-dedicated-sourcing-playbook-v1.pdf (architecture options), sla-pricing-estimate.xlsx (placeholder numbers we’ll refine after sizing).

Please reply with preferred workshop date and any other folks you want included (security / legal / ops). I’ll lock the invite and loop in the right product/ops folks on our side.

Thanks,

Marissa Cole

Marissa — thanks for the clear recap. Quick notes:

- Sep 22 works for an initial 90m workshop (10:00–11:30 PT) — please send a calendar invite.
- We will include our security lead (Daniel Park) and one engineer (Rita Gomez). Procurement (procurement@heliogenlabs.com) will attend for the cost discussion.

- KMS: we prefer a bring-your-own-key flow (AWS KMS) — is that supported for Private deployments or Dedicated?

Also: are you able to run a short micro-benchmark in the workshop (20m) so our engineers can see p50/p95 under representative prompts?

Looking forward — Alice

FYI forwarding HelioGen replies — prepping numbers. Quick notes for the playbook:
- Preliminary sizing: 4 H100-equivalent nodes should meet the stated steady-state (2–3M tokens/day + 200 qps sustained). Add 2-node burst for nightly batch and heavy retrain inference.
- Expected latency envelope after tuning: p50 ~ 45–70ms, p95 ~ 220–360ms depending on sequence length; micro-benchmark in workshop to validate.
- Cost sketch: rough ballpark for 4-node reserved pool + ops/support (monthly): see attached sla-pricing-estimate.xlsx. We’ll refine with exact SKU and region.
- KMS/BYOK: supported for Dedicated and Private (we’ll include ops runbook for key rotation and audit).

Next steps for team:
1) Prepare a 20m micro-benchmark script and sample prompts (owner: sales-eng).
2) Ops to prepare isolation runbook summary and audit log retention options (owner: ops).
3) Update the SLA bullets to include 99.9% uptime and clear latency targets with credits (owner: Ben).
